_note: Voiceover for the TradingQuiz SPY cup-and-handle zoom reel. The FIRST cut of this script ran 74.7s against a 36s reel, so the picture is now derived from the measured audio instead of the other way round: synthesise, measure, then size each act to what was actually said. Keep lines short — every extra clause costs a second of reel.

segments.text: This is the S and P five hundred. Real daily bars.
Now watch what happens when we pull the camera back.
That same line, again and again. Ten tests since twenty twenty one. That is what turns a drawn line into a level.
And price just closed back above it, on a cup and handle. Five seconds. Call it.
Buy. Your entry is the close that reclaimed the rim. Four forty point six one.
Now the stop. Under the handle, because if price falls back into the cup, the setup never happened. Being wrong costs eight dollars and eight cents.
The target is arithmetic, not hope. One to two risk appetite. You risked eight, so you aim sixteen. Four fifty six point seven six.
Both ends set. Let it run.
Target hit. Plus three point seven percent.
Not every cup and handle reaches its target. That is exactly why the stop is set before the entry.
Like and follow for more setups.

_speed_note: atempo 1.15x. The rate is chosen from a syllable target, not by ear: ep.1 was approved at 3.89 syl/s and a short was rejected at 4.64 as 'truncated and artificial' (commit 2b0aa60). Raw narration here runs 3.49, so 1.15x lands 4.02 - above the approved register for pace, well under the rejected one. atempo, never rubberband: measured word-error damage is +0.000 up to 1.38x, while rubberband drifts >4kHz energy 20.6% at 1.30x and that drift IS the metallic edge.
